title: Quality / accuracy benchmark result
description: One quality evaluation of one candidate against one dataset - the output of scripts/validate_tool_calling.py (BFCL) and scripts/validate_mmlu.py (MMLU). Deliberately a SEPARATE schema from benchmark_result.schema.json: docs/note.md §5 keeps the quality and performance layers independently measurable, and §34 warns against collapsing them into a single score before the trade-off has been characterised. The two are joined at analysis time on `model_config_key`, not merged at write time. Self-contained (no cross-file $ref). Conformance levels: see schemas/README.md - the current scripts emit a flatter row than this, and docs/TODO.md Phase 5 is where they are brought into conformance.

_comment.description: Optional free-text annotation. JSON has no comment syntax, and the example documents in schemas/examples/ need to say plainly that their numbers are illustrative rather than measured - a caveat that must travel with the file, not sit in a README nobody opens next to it. Ignored by every consumer; never carries data.

result_id.description: Traceable back to (model config, dataset version, git commit) the same way a benchmark_result's experiment_id is.

manifest.description: Reduced form of benchmark_result's manifest. A quality score is as backend-dependent as a latency number - both of this lab's known tool-calling failures (llama.cpp's temperature sensitivity, Bielik's empty tool_calls on vLLM) are backend/version effects, not model effects, and would be uninterpretable without this block.

model_config_key.description: Key into configs/models.yaml - the join key against benchmark_result documents.

backend.description: Added 'edge-llm' 2026-09-10. configs/models.yaml has carried edge-llm rows since 2026-09-08 and model.schema.json was updated to accept them, but BOTH result schemas were missed - so every Edge-LLM result this lab has ever produced, including the campaign behind its own recommendation, failed validation on this enum alone. That is a large part of what docs/TODO.md means by Thor's documents 'failing both result schemas'; it was a one-word omission, not a design decision.

backend_version.description: From the running server. llama.cpp build 4579 rejects tool_choice outright while 5058 does not, so a tool-calling score without a build number is unattributable.

execution_condition.description: Which board state produced this score. NOT required yet, and that is a recorded gap rather than a judgement that it does not matter: benchmark_result.schema.json has made this a first-class REQUIRED field since Phase 2, while every quality result written before 2026-09-10 carried the condition only inside the free-text `manifest.command` string, where no validator could reach it. The guard (benchmarks/manifest.py:assert_condition_matches_reality) did run for those results - scripts/validate_tool_calling.py has always required --execution-condition - so the label was enforced, just never structured. Made optional so the 25 already-conforming Orin results stay valid; promote to `required` once they are backfilled (docs/TODO.md Phase 5).

co_resident_with.description: What else ran, when execution_condition is 'co-resident'. Same completeness rule the perf side enforces: a declared workload a reader trusts to be complete is exactly as load-bearing as the top-level label (docs/HISTORY.md Phase 3, incident 3 - five results named vllm-orchestrator but not tts_consumer.py and had to be corrected in place).

backend.description: Added 'edge-llm' 2026-09-10. configs/models.yaml has carried edge-llm rows since 2026-09-08 and model.schema.json was updated to accept them, but BOTH result schemas were missed - so every Edge-LLM result this lab has ever produced, including the campaign behind its own recommendation, failed validation on this enum alone. That is a large part of what docs/TODO.md means by Thor's documents 'failing both result schemas'; it was a one-word omission, not a design decision.

tool_call_parser.description: vLLM's --tool-call-parser, when tool calling was evaluated. A first-class result axis here: `hermes` and `llama3_json` both score 0 for Bielik on vLLM while llama.cpp's grammar-constrained path scores well on the same model.

dataset.description: docs/note.md §20 - a dataset without a version is not a reproducible evaluation, and a silently modified dataset invalidates every comparison drawn against it.

version.description: Dataset release, e.g. BFCL_v3. Bumped on any change to the staged corpus.

n_available.description: Cases in the staged corpus - e.g. 399 BFCL simple + 239 irrelevance, 14042 MMLU all/test.

n_evaluated.description: Cases actually scored. Required alongside n_available so a sampled run can never be mistaken for a full one: this lab's only real BFCL scorecard so far is n=40 of 638, and that context is the difference between a data point and a claim.

sampling_method.description: How n_evaluated was drawn. `first-n` (the --limit flag's behaviour) is not a random sample and must not be described as one.

preprocessing_version.description: docs/note.md §20. Bumped whenever the loader changes what the model sees. Not bookkeeping: BFCL's own non-standard JSON-schema type names ("float" x215, "tuple" x2, "any" x1) crash llama.cpp's grammar builder and are rewritten by this repo's loader - two runs either side of that fix are not comparable.

prompt_template_version.description: docs/note.md §21 - the chat template materially changes behaviour and is therefore an experimental variable.

protocol.description: How scoring was performed. docs/note.md §41 requires the same evaluation protocol across compared candidates, which is only checkable if the protocol is recorded rather than assumed.

scorer.description: Which scorer produced these numbers, stated precisely enough that the score is not mistaken for an official leaderboard figure. This repo uses a simplified AST-style checker, not the official `bfcl-eval` package, and generative letter-parsing for MMLU rather than logprob scoring (which would need a backend-specific API and so could not compare vLLM against llama.cpp at all).

temperature.description: Pinned, and material. At llama.cpp's server default (~0.8) Qwen2.5-1.5B emits a correct tool call 12/15 times; at 0.1 it is 15/15, while vLLM is 15/15 at both. A tool-calling score without its temperature is not a property of the model.

tool_choice.description: "auto" for this lab's tool-calling eval: the point is measuring UNFORCED judgment, so orchestrator.py's forced-tool_choice production workaround is deliberately not used here.

repetitions.description: Times the whole set was evaluated. >1 enables the mean/stddev/CI reporting docs/note.md §32 allows for stochastic evaluation - which is the only context where a mean belongs in this repo at all.

top_p.description: Nucleus truncation, recorded for the same reason as `temperature`: pinning temperature ALONE is not controlled sampling, because the backends ship different truncation defaults (Edge-LLM top_p=0.9/top_k=50, vLLM top_p=1.0/top_k=-1). On a tool-call ABSTENTION decision that is not cosmetic - a 0.9 nucleus can drop a low-probability <tool_call> start that an untruncated sampler emits. Added 2026-09-10, after scripts/validate_tool_calling.py had been writing this field since the 2026-09-09 cross-backend campaign and every result it produced consequently failed validation against this schema.

top_k.description: Top-k truncation. Same reasoning as `top_p`. `top_k=1` is this lab's greedy control: with one surviving candidate token, top_p/min_p/temperature are all inert, so all three backends decode deterministically and identically-configured - which is what made the decoding hypothesis falsifiable.

scores.description: Accuracy figures, always with the sample count they were computed over (docs/note.md §32: score, n, benchmark version - never a bare percentage).

by_category.description: Per-category breakdown; for BFCL, `simple` and `irrelevance` measure opposite error directions and their average alone hides which way a model fails.

confidence_interval_95.description: Only where statistically meaningful. docs/note.md §32 also warns against excessive decimal precision - an interval implied by n=40 is wide, and rounding should show that.

tool_call_outcomes.description: docs/note.md §36 - tool calling reported as a confusion matrix plus failure taxonomy, not one percentage. The distinction that matters for embedded-ai-chain is between a model that calls the wrong tool and one that calls a tool when it should have answered directly: the second wastes an escalation the orchestrator did not need, which is exactly embedded-ai-chain/docs/paper.md's P4 cost. Present only for tool-calling evaluations.

false_positive.description: No tool expected, tool called - the wasted-escalation case.

false_negative.description: Tool expected, none called - the missed-escalation case.

correct_tool.description: Right function chosen, among calls made.

correct_arguments.description: Right function AND right arguments. Strictly stronger than correct_tool; kept separate because argument extraction and tool selection fail for different reasons.

hallucinated_tool.description: A function name that was never offered.

formatting_failure.description: The model described wanting to call a tool in prose instead of emitting a structured call - the exact failure mode observed for Qwen2.5-1.5B on llama.cpp at default temperature, and for Bielik on vLLM under both parsers tried. A capability question and a formatting question have different fixes, so they are counted separately.

server_error.description: The request failed at the server (HTTP 500, grammar-conversion failure). A backend defect, not a model score - and one this lab has already hit twice.

outcomes_file.description: Path to the per-case raw outcomes, relative to the results root. Same principle as benchmark_result's `runs`: per-case data is preserved so a score can be re-derived and error analysis stays possible. Kept out-of-line only because a full BFCL corpus is 638 cases and a full MMLU run is 14042.
